questions.question_description: Implement Breadth First Search (BFS) for an undirected graph. Given N vertices, M edges, and a source vertex S, print the BFS traversal.
questions.input_format: Integers N and M, followed by M lines of edges 'u v'. Followed by the source vertex S.
questions.output_format: Space-separated BFS traversal. Start from S. Visit neighbors in increasing order of their vertex IDs.
questions.hints: Use a queue. Enqueue the starting node, mark as visited. Dequeue, print, enqueue unvisited adjacent nodes in order.
questions.solution_explanation: BFS systematically visits all nodes connected to S in rings, checking neighbors layer by layer using a Queue.

questions.question_description: Implement Depth First Search (DFS) for an undirected graph. Given N vertices, M edges, and a source vertex S, print the DFS traversal.
questions.input_format: Integers N and M, followed by M lines of edges 'u v'. Followed by the source vertex S.
questions.output_format: Space-separated DFS traversal. Start from S. Visit neighbors in increasing order of their vertex IDs recursively.
questions.hints: Use recursion or a stack. Start at node S, mark it as visited, print it, and recursively perform DFS on its first unvisited adjacent node.
questions.solution_explanation: DFS explores as far down a path as possible before backtracking. We can achieve this elegantly using the call stack in recursion.
